title: Drag and drop of files into a desktop window
when: Users want to drag documents or images from the file manager into the desktop app window to open or import them.
prompt:
Goal: drop.js accepts files dropped anywhere on the window, highlights the target, filters types and imports each file with feedback.
Steps:
1. On document, listen to dragenter and dragover with event.preventDefault() so the WebView does not navigate to the file; set event.dataTransfer.dropEffect = "copy".
2. Show an overlay on dragenter; count enter and leave events so child elements do not make it flicker.
3. On drop: preventDefault, hide the overlay, take [...event.dataTransfer.files].
4. Filter by extension and size (for example .csv and .json under 20 MB); list skipped files with the reason.
5. Read content with await file.text() or file.arrayBuffer() and pass it to the importer; process files one by one with a progress line.
6. Do not rely on a full file path from the drop: the WebView usually hides it; to save back to the same file, ask with the Save dialog.
7. Keep a visible "Import files" button that opens Neutralino.os.showOpenDialog for keyboard and accessibility users.
8. Announce the result in an aria-live region: "3 files imported, 1 skipped".
Quality bar:
- Dropping an unsupported file never navigates away from the app.
- Large drops show progress and stay responsive.
Pitfalls:
- Forgetting preventDefault on dragover, which disables drop.
- Reading all files at once into memory.
Verify:
- [ ] dragover and drop call preventDefault.
- [ ] Types and sizes are filtered.
- [ ] A button alternative exists.
Output: drop.js, overlay markup and styles.

examples.input: arrastar planilhas CSV pra dentro do app desktop
examples.output: Window wide drop overlay, type and size filter, file.text import queue, aria-live summary, Import button
